scope: Proposition 9.7 (Matching of all positive-diameter clusters) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 97. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every positive-diameter Hausdorff limit of lattice free-current clusters is one retained canonical cluster, and every retained canonical cluster is the limit of its visible precursor. No distinct invisible precursor has a positive-diameter limit. The same assertions hold for the free primal descendants after the wired layer, jointly with that layer and the height. Consequently Ff ∗ = F(Cf ), Fw ∗ = F(Cw ), and both collections converge in the matching topology of Theorem 2.3.
